A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PF decoding and watermarking work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison despite reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original text-generation and watermark-detection experiments on C4 and Alpaca, including attack and text-length evaluations in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds KGW watermark configurations and results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain the same PF sampling procedure, exponential-noise watermark generation, detection statistic, and Gamma-based threshold. Renaming logit robustness as stability does not change the proposed methods.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate C4 completion and Alpaca question answering, with the same paraphrasing, deletion, and text-length scenarios. Added KGW configurations reuse this coverage; the new safety examples are mathematical illustrations, not additional empirical tasks.

E2.justification: The attack comparison expands from KGW with a four-token prefix, Gumbel, and PF in v1 Table 3 to include an additional KGW one-token-prefix variant in v2 Table 4. Existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: Additional KGW experiments introduce single-token hashing and green-list fractions of 0.1 and 0.25, with watermark strength 2.0 and temperatures from 0.2 to 1.0. These are added configurations; the retained experiments' data selection, generation limits, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 extends the existing attack analysis with KGW's one-token-prefix configuration and adds Appendix C.3 sensitivity comparisons across KGW green-list fractions and temperatures. The earlier attack tests and PF text-length analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report perplexity standard errors after removing the highest and lowest 3% of scores, and retain the same four random-key false-positive-rate curves. The added KGW results introduce no new uncertainty or repeated-run reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v2 Tables 4, 6, and 7 add KGW configuration results. Table 2 also changes the C4, T=0.8 greedy row: PPL1/PPL2 change from 1.14/1.24 to 1.28/1.75, repetition from 0.56 to 0.12, and MAUVE from 0.05 to 0.93, without an explanatory setting change. Other matched empirical results are retained.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the Gumbel harmonic-number arguments in Example 4.5 and adds explicit non-stability counterexamples in Appendix B.2. The main theorems and existing proofs remain unchanged; the diversity remark is relocated. Some added reasoning is erroneous: the two greedy-example logit vectors have the same maximizing token.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same PF tradeoff guarantees, distribution-preserving watermark claim, false-positive control, and empirical detection-quality claims. The robustness-to-stability terminology change preserves their mathematical scope.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 expands the earlier brief safety motivation into a gray-box logit-bias threat model and argues that PF can make jailbreaking harder. Appendix C.1 explicitly distinguishes watermark resilience to removal attacks from logit stability.

D1.justification: v2 documents the added KGW hashing and hyperparameter configurations and changes the reported GPU designation from Nvidia A600 to A6000. Existing data-processing instructions, sample counts, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds a citation to OpenAI's logit-bias documentation to motivate the API threat model. The scholarly bibliography and positioning relative to earlier PF sampling, differential privacy, and watermarking research otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 consistently substitutes stability for logit robustness, makes localized wording edits, updates affiliations, and removes the contents page. It moves the diversity remark into the new stability appendix while retaining the main section sequence and most existing prose.

P2.justification: The conference layout substantially reorganizes displays: v1 Figures 2–3 become v2 Figure 2's panels, Figures 4–5 become Figure 3's panels, and Table 2 changes from stacked dataset blocks to a much smaller two-by-two arrangement. v2 also adds Tables 3, 6, and 7 and revises figure placement and captions.

improvement.justification: The added KGW comparisons address baseline sensitivity, and Example 4.5 corrects a formula. However, new Appendix B examples contain incorrect greedy and Top-k reasoning, while Table 2 replaces the C4 greedy row with values matching the Alpaca row without explanation. These evaluation gains coexist with new mathematical and reporting defects, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
